Chapter 185: Professionals Creating Professional Content

Saturday.

The ever-frugal Great Hero Chen finally got a new phone.

He had to support his own company's mobile version of Weibo, after all.

It was inexcusable to expect users to post on Weibo from their phones when he wasn't even doing it himself.

"I want the silver one, you get the black one," Bian Guanyue said, picking through them.

"Alright," Chen Guiliang smiled. "A matching set."

The two of them each bought a Nokia N70, costing 4500 yuan apiece.

Chen Guiliang swapped in his own SIM card and sent a text message to 10086 to activate GPRS service. Then, he subscribed to a monthly plan for Weibo's SMS and MMS services, long-pressed the 0 key to enter Monternet, and typed in Kaixin Net's WAP URL.

He composed a Weibo post: "Got a new phone, I can take pictures now. A memento for my first post."

He clicked to send the text and a selfie.

Just two days prior, both China Mobile and China Unicom had changed their rules: for unlimited value-added services, SMS and MMS messages would only be charged for sending; receiving messages would no longer incur a fee. A few individual provinces, however, still charged for receiving.

For Weibo, this was practically a godsend!

As long as a Weibo user enabled their GPRS service, they could receive text-only messages (as SMS) and posts with photos (as MMS) from the people they followed without spending a single cent.

Unfortunately, this proto-Weibo was an incomplete version, making it difficult to interact on a large scale via mobile phone.

Its interaction process was as follows: a user follows someone → that person sends a Weibo post from their phone → the user receives an SMS and MMS.

It was entirely one-way output, unable to form effective feedback.

If fans wanted to comment or forward, they could only do so by logging in on a computer.

Moreover, if the person being followed posted on Weibo from a computer, their followers would only receive the text on their phones and not the photos via MMS.

"Congratulations, congratulations."

Ao Yanchen received the Weibo post, which had been converted into a mobile text message, and directly replied with a congratulatory text to Chen Guiliang's phone.

Chen Guiliang asked, "How are things on your end?"

Ao Yanchen replied, "Boring to death. Speeches from the leaders, presentations from peers, then more speeches from the leaders, and more presentations from peers. I have to give a presentation too... Just signed a 'China Internet Association Copyright Alliance Agreement'."

Chen Guiliang: "Tough on you."

Ao Yanchen: "Can't chat, I'm about to head into a breakout session."

The 2005 China Internet Conference was currently underway. It was being held just eight kilometers from Chen Guiliang's company.

Chen Guiliang did not attend in person.

Because he had looked at the conference agenda and found it utterly boring.

But he had to send someone, as a host of leaders from the China Association for Science and Technology, the Ministry of Information Industry, and other bodies would be in attendance. So, Ao Yanchen went to fill in for him.

The bosses of the major domestic internet companies felt pretty much the same way as Chen Guiliang.

Aside from Netease, Sina, and Sohu, the other companies sent a vice president at most. Shanda and Alibaba didn't even send a VP.

As for the first three, the reason their CEOs attended in person was that they were there to receive an award... the Industry Self-Discipline Contribution Award.

After fiddling with her phone for a bit, Bian Guanyue said excitedly, "I posted on Weibo too. It's a shame I can't see forwards and comments on my phone."

"Yeah, it would be great if the computer and mobile web pages could communicate," Chen Guiliang mused.

That technology would have to wait another two years, only beginning to sprout after the first-generation iPhone was released.

And for the technology to achieve a further breakthrough, one would have to wait until after 2010!

If Chen Guiliang had the money to organize a research and development team and invest a massive amount of capital into this specific technology, he might be able to make a breakthrough a year or a year and a half earlier.

The two walked side by side out of the Pacific Building. Chen Guiliang asked, "How many followers do you have on Kaixin Net?"

"Over 5,000," Bian Guanyue smiled. "They're all my fans, especially fans of 'The Wind Rises'."

Chen Guiliang showed off, "I have over 80,000 followers."

"I know." Bian Guanyue observed it every day, paying more attention to the changes in his follower count than he did.

*Those Things in the Ming Dynasty* had stopped updating on all forums and blogs. Only Chen Guiliang's accounts on Xiaonei Net and Kaixin Net were still serializing it in the form of blog entries.

Of his 80,000-plus followers, a portion were actually freeloader book fans—the serialized content had been published long ago, but these freeloaders couldn't even be bothered to buy a pirated copy, opting to slowly follow the free updates online instead.

The vast majority of the remaining followers were recommended by Kaixin Net.

Unlocking one lock after another, Bian Guanyue sat on the back of the bicycle, and Chen Guiliang pedaled hard, riding off.

Kaixin Net's announcement of signing Zhang Liangying as their spokesperson didn't attract much attention from Sina Blog.

Because Sina Blog's direct competitors were the dozen or so major and minor blog brands of the time.

The one that was truly nervous was Ruolin Net!

This website was founded several months before Xiaonei Net.

At this very moment, the two founders of Ruolin Net were sitting in their office, discussing the situation.

One was Chen Haoyuan, responsible for strategy, financing, and operations.

The other was Zou Lin, responsible for technology, products, and marketing.

"We really can't compete with Kaixin Net," Zou Lin said. "Kaixin Net has Xiaonei Net funneling traffic to it, they've invited a bunch of celebrities, and they're attracting users with 'Happy Farm' and 'Parking Wars'. It's only been online for a little over a month, and their user numbers are about to catch up to ours. We've been at this for over a year!"

Chen Haoyuan said, "Our user bases are still different. We focus on business professionals, especially the urban white-collar class. Theirs are mainly students, celebrities, fans, and ordinary netizens."

"How do we differentiate ourselves to compete?" Zou Lin asked.

Chen Haoyuan said, "It used to be social networking first, recruitment second. From now on, it will be recruitment first, social networking second. We can't compete with Kaixin Net on the social front anymore, we just can't win."

Zou Lin asked, "Why don't we also make a few casual social games?"

Chen Haoyuan shook his head. "Let's not get distracted by making games. It's too low-brow. After all, our users are business professionals and white-collar workers!"

Ruolin Net, a perfectly fine mainstream social networking site, was being forced by Chen Guiliang to pivot into a recruitment website. Besides recruitment, it also offered features like building connections, maintaining business relationships, expanding business opportunities, and industry exchanges.

This was precisely the development path of the neighboring Tianji Net.

From the very beginning, Tianji Net had forgone broad social networking features to focus on business-oriented ones. By being forced to pivot, Ruolin Net was now poised for a head-on, cutthroat battle with Tianji Net.

"There's news!" Xie Yang came into Chen Guiliang's office with Li Fan.

Chen Guiliang asked, "What news?"

Xie Yang said, "Sina Blog has invited too many celebrities. Especially the pop stars, more than half of them are people we couldn't get. It's not about how much money we throw at them; stars aren't short on that kind of cash. So I had someone look into it, and Li Fan got results very quickly."

"Amazing, Li Shijie," Chen Guiliang praised.

Li Fan said, "I worked at iResearch for a few months, so I know a little about information analysis. I also interned at four media companies, so I have a slight understanding of the media circle. The reason Sina Blog was able to invite so many stars is all thanks to an entertainment reporter named Liu Xuan. Same name as the Olympic champion Liu Xuan."

"An entertainment reporter?" Chen Guiliang genuinely didn't know.

Li Fan said, "This reporter is very famous in the industry. She used to work at a foreign bank, then became an editor for a fashion magazine, and later took charge of the magazine's film section. She often interviews directors, stars, and bosses, and is also a professional film critic."

"At the end of last year, she was hired by Sina's entertainment section. As soon as she joined Sina, she was appointed head of reporters for the entertainment section and interviewed a large number of stars in a short period of time."

"Xu Jinglei, who just joined Sina Blog, met Liu Xuan during an interview, and now they've become best friends. They even have daily photos together, which they used to post on other blog sites."

Xie Yang lamented, "It really takes a professional. People like Xu Jinglei and Fan Bingbing, we can't even get a meeting with them, let alone invite them to Kaixin Net. But as soon as this entertainment reporter Liu Xuan made a move, Xu Jinglei and Fan Bingbing both agreed to join Sina Blog!"

"Then let's hire another professional," Chen Guiliang said.

This kind of professional was not easy to find.

There were plenty of entertainment reporters and film critics, but someone who could become best friends with the stars they interviewed was definitely a rare find.

Li Fan suggested, "Why don't we find someone from a fashion magazine too? They have contact with stars and also understand fashion content. Kaixin Net has a growing number of white-collar users, so we can create more fashion-related topics. Introducing foreign fashion brands, basic fashion knowledge, teaching people how to dress, match outfits, and do makeup... the urban female users would definitely love that."

Chen Guiliang smiled. "That could work."

Xie Yang added, "We could also invite one... no need to hire directly, but invite well-known military and sports reporters or editors to create accounts on Kaixin Net. For every professional military or sports article they write, we'll pay them a fee that's slightly higher than the market rate. This way, they can gain followers and earn money, so they'll definitely be willing to cooperate long-term. There are a lot of male netizens who love military and sports topics!"

Chen Guiliang thought seriously for a moment. "Let's do it your way. Establish a system for specially invited contributors instead of hiring them as direct employees. And it won't be limited to fashion, entertainment, military, and sports content. We can invite a few contributors from various industries for long-term collaboration. As for their payment, we'll calculate it based on their articles' click-through rates."

Sina Blog was making a big move, and Kaixin Net had to compete on content as well.

After Xie Yang and Li Fan left, Chen Guiliang picked up his mouse and clicked open Sina Blog.

Celebrities are lazy, especially when they are forced to do business.

Super Girls like Li Yuchun and Zhou Bichang had already deleted their Kaixin Net accounts and collectively moved to Sina Blog. This was clearly the work of Tianyu Media, which must have taken money from Sina Blog.

Only Zhang Liangying, as the spokesperson for Kaixin Net, remained.

But the Super Girls were extremely busy with activities; they simply didn't have the energy to write articles. The blogs of Li Yuchun and the others were all written by their management company, and the content was nothing but promotion.

If not for the accompanying photos, their fans would probably be cursing up a storm over these cookie-cutter promotional articles.

Fan Bingbing's blog was much the same, full of promotional articles not written by herself at all.

Writers like Yu Qiuyu, Yu Hua, and Han Han were even more interesting. Although they had agreed to open blogs on Sina, they hadn't posted a single article to date. Because they had no time.

The fanfare was huge, but the results so far were minimal.

Only Xu Jinglei was a true powerhouse. This actress actually wrote her own posts. And she loved to write, updating with high frequency and always including her own beautiful photos with every post. She brought a massive amount of traffic to Sina Blog!

(End of Chapter)
